g.text: Trade Restrictiveness Index by technology and supply-chain stage, all suppliers, August
2026 Census duty plus AD/CVD cash deposits. The highest walls stand at solar assembly
(39%), gas assembly (36%), oil assembly (34%); extraction and fuel refining are mostly
Where has America actually built tariff walls?
* Deployment has no traded goods of its own: it is scored on the technology's Assembly basket (the goods the build-out
imports), so it repeats the Assembly value.
Italic value with a dot: thin cell (under $0.5bn of 2024 imports). –: no traded basket goods at this stage. AD/CVD lines are
Trade Restrictiveness Index (Waugh): the uniform tariff with the same welfare cost as the actual tariff structure, sqrt(sum
w*t^2 / sum w) on 2024 import weights. It rises with dispersion as well as level; it is not an average tariff and should not be
multiplied by imports to estimate revenue.
Source: NEIS analysis of US Census Bureau imports for consumption and calculated duty by HTS-10 line and partner (via the Trade
War Tracker, github.com/tradewartracker), Commerce AD/CVD notices in the Federal Register.
